findings.title: Hardcoded 10MB client-side limit breaks max_attachment_size_kb for non-image uploads
findings.body: validateUploadedFile is called for both images and attachments (type is 'image' or 'attachment'). The previous code used Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'] so attachment uploads respected SiteSetting.max_attachment_size_kb. The change to a hardcoded 10MB means any admin who has set max_attachment_size_kb to anything larger than 10MB will see those legitimate attachment uploads rejected client-side, even though the server side still allows them. The intended behavior of letting oversized images through for downsizing should only apply to images, not attachments, since attachments are not downsized in this PR.

findings.title: FileHelper.download limit raised to 10.megabytes, allowing oversized URL fetches
findings.body: The download cap was changed from SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes (e.g. 4MB) to a hardcoded 10.megabytes. The only motivation is to fetch a larger image so it can be downsized locally. As a side effect, the server will now happily fetch up to 10MB from any URL the API caller supplies (and then potentially store a 10MB file even if the configured max_image_size_kb is, say, 500KB, if the downsize loop fails to bring it down). For sites that intentionally keep max_image_size_kb small to limit storage, this widens both bandwidth and disk exposure. The cap should stay tied to (or be a multiple of) SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb, not unconditionally 10MB.

findings.title: Downsize loop silently proceeds if file cannot be reduced under max_image_size_kb
findings.body: After up to 5 iterations of OptimizedImage.downsize at 80%, the loop only checks tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes. The return value of OptimizedImage.downsize (which can be false if convert/gifsicle fails) is ignored, so an unsupported/corrupt image produces no error. More importantly, if the loop exhausts attempts and the file is still above max_image_size_kb, the code falls through and calls Upload.create_for anyway, so an oversized file is stored with no feedback to the user. The user has spent bandwidth uploading a file that should have been rejected. Either surface an error if the loop ends without success, or break out and skip the upload.

findings.title: OptimizedImage.downsize is invoked with source and destination pointing at the same tempfile path
findings.body: OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, '80%', ...) reads from and writes to the same file. ImageMagick's convert typically needs to fully open the input before writing the output, and on many filesystems this fails or corrupts the source. Use a separate Tempfile for the destination and move it back over the original on success.

findings.title: Duplicate def self.downsize redefines the public API and silently breaks 5-argument callers
findings.body: The file now contains two def self.downsize definitions. In Ruby the second definition (line 149) completely replaces the first (line 145), so the 5-argument form downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={}) is now dead and unreachable. Any caller that still uses the 5-argument signature (plugins, jobs, or other internal code) will instead hit the 4-argument version downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={}), which interprets the third positional argument as a dimensions string (e.g. "100") rather than a width, and the fourth as opts (so a hash expected for opts will receive an integer and crash on opts[:allow_animation]). Either remove the unused first definition, or keep the 5-argument form as the canonical signature and remove the new 4-argument overload.

findings.title: Dead downsize definition left in place after refactor
findings.body: After the refactor, the 5-argument def self.downsize on line 145 is unreachable because line 149 redefines the same method with a different signature. Keeping the dead body around invites future maintainers to call it (and get the broken behavior described in the API finding above) or to waste time understanding which form is active. Delete it.
